sections.h2: What is an eviction in Oklahoma, and who can order one?
sections.html:
An eviction in Oklahoma is a court case called Forcible Entry and Detainer, or FED, and only a judge can order a tenant out. Legal Aid Services of Oklahoma notes that a landlord cannot change the locks or shut off water, heat, electricity or gas first, even when rent is unpaid.

Most residential cases are heard in small claims court, according to Legal Aid Services of Oklahoma. The landlord usually asks for possession of the house, a money judgment for unpaid rent and damage, or both.

For anyone who owns a rented house in Oklahoma and wants to sell it, this matters because the sale does not pause or replace the court process. The case runs on the tenant's notice dates and the court calendar, not on the closing date.

sections.h2: Which written notice has to come first?
sections.html:
The notice depends on why the landlord wants the tenant gone, and Title 41 sets a different clock for each reason. A court filing without the right notice is usually where a landlord's case goes wrong.

SituationNotice or time periodWhere it comes from
Rent not paid5 days after written demand; the demand also counts as a demand for possession41 O.S. 131(B)
Lease breach that can be fixedWritten notice giving 10 days to fix it, with the tenancy ending 15 days after receipt if not fixed41 O.S. 132(B)
Month-to-month or at-will tenancy30 days written notice from either side41 O.S. 111
Tenancy shorter than month-to-month7 days written notice41 O.S. 111
Fire, flood or similar emergency caused by tenant24 to 48 hours written noticeLegal Aid Services of Oklahoma
Drug-related or threatening crime24 hour written noticeLegal Aid Services of Oklahoma

A lease with a fixed end date simply expires on that date unless the parties agreed otherwise, so no notice is needed to end it.

sections.h2: How must the notice be delivered?
sections.html:
The landlord must deliver the notice by hand when the tenant can be found, and the statute gives two fallbacks. Section 111 allows delivery to a family member over twelve who lives with the tenant, and then posting on the door plus a mailed copy.

  • First choice: personal delivery to the tenant.
  • Second: a family member over age twelve living there.
  • Third: a copy posted in a visible spot on the home, with another copy mailed by certified mail or the Postal Service accountable mail book.

Legal Aid describes the same two routes in plain terms: post it and mail it, or hand it over through the landlord, a process server or the sheriff.

sections.h2: How fast does the case move after it is filed?
sections.html:
Fast. Under 12 O.S. 1148.4 the summons sets a trial between 5 and 10 days after it is issued, and it must state the claim and the amount the landlord will accept if the tenant does not appear.

Under 12 O.S. 1148.5 the tenant must be served at least three days before trial. The statute also allows leaving a copy with a resident over fifteen at the home, or certified mail postmarked at least three days before trial if reasonable efforts at hand delivery fail.

A tenant who skips the hearing risks a default judgment, which Legal Aid says means the landlord wins automatically.

sections.h2: What happens after the judge rules for the landlord?
sections.html:
After a judgment for possession, the landlord asks the court clerk for a writ of execution, and the sheriff or another officer carries it out. Under 12 O.S. 1148.10 the writ directs removal of the defendant, return of possession to the plaintiff and collection of rent, fees and costs.

  • A motion for a new trial has to be filed within three days and does not pause the writ.
  • Under 12 O.S. 1148.10A the officer or landlord warns the tenant that they will return in 48 hours, either in person or by a posted notice.
  • A tenant who refuses to give up the home when the writ is served commits a trespass offense with a fine of up to $500, up to 30 days in county jail, or both.
  • To appeal, the tenant may post a supersedeas bond within 2 days of judgment, which a judge can extend to no more than 7 days, and must keep paying current rent into the court clerk's office.

Missing a rent payment during an appeal is treated as giving up the appeal.

sections.h2: What if the landlord changes the locks without going to court?
sections.html:
A landlord who wrongfully removes or shuts out a tenant owes real money. Under 41 O.S. 123 the tenant can recover possession or end the rental agreement, and in either case recover up to twice the average monthly rent or twice actual damages, whichever is greater.

If the tenant ends the rental, the landlord must also return recoverable deposits and prepaid rent. Anyone planning to sell a tenant-occupied house should know that a lockout done to clear the home for a buyer creates a bigger problem than it solves.

sections.h2: What happens to belongings the tenant leaves behind?
sections.html:
Section 130 of Title 41 covers both abandonment and lawful removal after an eviction. If the landlord judges the items to have no apparent value, they may be disposed of with no duty to account for them.

If they do have apparent value, the landlord sends a written notice by certified mail to the last known address. Property left with the landlord for 30 days or longer is conclusively treated as abandoned. The landlord must keep stored items safe and use reasonable care, and may charge storage costs.

Where a tenant dies as the only occupant, 41 O.S. 130.1 sets a separate process for a designated contact, including a 30 day mailed request before discarding property.

sections.h2: How does an eviction case affect selling a rented house?
sections.html:
A sale does not end a tenancy. Under 41 O.S. 119 a landlord's conveyance of real estate is valid without the tenant's agreement, and rent paid to the seller before the tenant gets written notice of the sale counts as properly paid.

Once the tenant has written notice, future rent goes to the buyer. The seller is relieved of duties for events after that notice, and the successor takes on the obligations under the rental agreement.

Showings are possible but not unlimited. Section 128 lets a landlord enter to show the unit to prospective buyers, with at least one day's notice except in an emergency, and only at reasonable times.

sections.h2: What do owners of Oklahoma rental houses usually run into?
sections.html:
Oklahoma has 77 counties, and the largest by population are Oklahoma County (822,125) and Tulsa County (698,782), according to Wikipedia's county list. Cases are filed where the house sits, so an owner in Cleveland County and an owner in Comanche County deal with different court clerks and calendars.

  • A tenant on a month-to-month arrangement needs a full 30 days of written notice, which can outlast a buyer's closing window.
  • A tenant behind on rent may stay through hearing and appeal if rent is paid into court.
  • Property left behind in a house after a hearing means more time and storage obligations.
  • Storm damage is common in a state that averages about 62 tornadoes a year, and a damaged rental can raise habitability disputes before any eviction starts.

Owners who would rather skip the process sometimes sell the house as is, with the tenant in place, so the buyer inherits the lease and the court calendar.

faqs.q: How many days does an Oklahoma landlord have to give for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Five days after written demand. Under 41 O.S. 131(B), if the tenant does not pay within that period the landlord may terminate the rental agreement, and the demand also counts as the demand for possession.

faqs.q: Can a landlord evict a tenant without going to court?
faqs.a: No. Only a judge can order a tenant to leave, and 41 O.S. 123 lets a locked-out tenant recover up to twice the monthly rent or twice actual damages, whichever is greater.

faqs.q: How long does an Oklahoma eviction case take?
faqs.a: The trial date is set 5 to 10 days after the summons is issued, under 12 O.S. 1148.4. After a judgment for the landlord, the 48 hour return notice under 12 O.S. 1148.10A follows.

faqs.q: Can a tenant appeal an Oklahoma eviction judgment?
faqs.a: Yes, but quickly. The tenant may post a supersedeas bond within 2 days, which a judge can extend to no more than 7 days, and must keep paying current rent into court while the appeal runs.

faqs.q: Does selling a rented house in Oklahoma cancel the lease?
faqs.a: No. Under 41 O.S. 119 the sale is valid without the tenant's consent, the buyer takes over the landlord's obligations, and the tenant pays rent to the buyer after receiving written notice of the sale.

faqs.q: Can a landlord show a rented house to buyers?
faqs.a: Yes, with at least one day's notice at a reasonable time, unless there is an emergency. The tenant may not unreasonably refuse entry for showings under 41 O.S. 128.
